title: Greenpanel Industries Ltd - 542857 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Greenpanel Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 15.5% YoY to INR391 crore, but FY26 reported EBITDA fell to INR94.2 crore (6.3%) and PAT was negative INR29.1 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 MDF domestic volumes grew 29.5% YoY, while total MDF volumes grew 27.8% after exports stopped in March due to Middle East disruption. Operating EBITDA excluding FX and one-offs was INR35.4 crore (9.1%) in Q4 and INR132.7 crore (8.8%) for FY26, while reported EBITDA was INR94.2 crore (6.3%) after a INR49 crore Euro-borrowing FX loss and new-line inefficiencies. Management announced a 15% MDF price increase (5% plus 10%) in response to chemical costs up 40-45%, but gave no numerical FY27 guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty and early signs of discounting.

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Domestic volume +29.5% YoY in Q4 and +16.9% for FY26; total volume +27.8% in Q4 and +12.9% in FY26. High-value products were 43% of volume and 55% of value in FY26.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 18% YoY in Q4 but were roughly flat for FY26. Plywood EBITDA margin was about 4%, and a 6% price increase was taken from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance given; management aims for volume growth as the primary goal, targeting market-level growth or better and stable-to-higher market share.
Industry demand expected to grow in early double digits to mid-teens in FY27.
Margin guidance withheld; management will 'sit out' Q1 FY27 before giving definitive margin guidance. Aim is to maintain or improve FY26 high-single-digit margin.

The 15% MDF price increase (5%+10%) is said to cover cost inflation so far, but full effect is not expected in Q1 FY27 due to phased implementation, trickle-in of old-price dispatches and early discounting.
Capex for FY27 limited to sustenance, INR20-30 crore; no major capex announcement planned this year, with evaluation next year. Focus on debt reduction.
Remaining EPCG benefit (about INR26 crore) expected in FY27 if exports recover; otherwise partly carried into FY28.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 60% in Q4 FY26 (55-60% annual), leaving headroom for organic growth without material investment.
Industry MDF capacity is 4 to 4.5 million cubic metres per annum; industry demand is estimated at about 3 million cubic metres in FY26 (15% growth assumed).
Two new capacities (Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh, about 400,000 cubic metres in total) are expected in H2 FY27 with calibrated ramp-up.
Greenpanel's three MDF lines are fungible; there is no dedicated thin MDF line. Thin MDF is about 25% of the market (750-800 thousand cubic metres).
Plywood expansion options are under consideration (minimal-investment addition at an existing site, or a new location), but only after existing capacity is fully utilised.
demand_pricing: Demand is muted. Pre-price-hike stocking happened in March, April was muted, and only priority projects are executing.
Chemicals (40-45% of raw material cost) rose 40-45%. Timber costs are stable, with multiple species now used instead of eucalyptus.
Early discounting is emerging: an industry leader reportedly offers 4.5-5% dealer discounts, which management says are target- or geography-based and partly offset by benefits.
Exports were nil for the whole of March due to freight issues linked to the Middle East war.
B2B sales to large-format OEMs are about 15-20% of volume (7,000-8,000 cubic metres per month); the rest goes through retail.
Industry volume grew mid-teens to high-teens in FY26 per management's estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance for MDF volume growth and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numeric guidance. It expects industry growth of early double digits to mid-teens, aims to match or beat the market, and intends to maintain or improve high-single-digit margins.

qa_highlights.question: Has the 15% price hike absorbed all cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has just about absorbed current cost inflation, but slight discounting has already started, so the full 15% is not yet in place.

qa_highlights.question: Why was domestic volume flat QoQ in Q4 despite March stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 volumes were held back to sell expensive inventory at higher post-hike prices, and that exports were zero in March. Nine-month domestic volume grew about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% price increase be fully visible in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Not necessarily. Implementation was phased, old-price dispatches trickled into April, and some discounting is underway, so the full effect is not assured in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is limited to sustenance, about INR20-30 crore. Growth capex will be evaluated next year, and the focus this year is on debt reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why was thin MDF capacity underutilised in FY26 after imports fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its three lines are fungible and not dedicated to thin MDF, and that everyone in India now produces thin MDF.

risks_watch: Middle East war: export shutdown (nil in March) and freight constraints; EPCG benefit depends on export recovery.
Chemical price volatility (up 40-45%); management says a further price hike is possible if costs rise substantially.
Competitive discounting by the industry leader could erode the 15% price increase and pressure margins.
Euro-denominated borrowing FX losses (INR49 crore in FY26) continue to affect reported profit.
Receivable days rose to 21 from 11 in FY25; watch whether this reflects dealer credit terms or March-end timing.
New capacity additions (about 400,000 cubic metres in H2 FY27) could add supply pressure.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on forward-looking items: management explicitly withheld FY27 volume and margin guidance and said it will wait out Q1 FY27 because of chemical costs, exports and pricing uncertainty. It was confident on FY26 operating delivery, the balance sheet and the 9-month volume build-up.
